the superluminescence in a plate-shaped active element of a neodymium glass laser is an undesirable phenomenon, which can reduce the energy stored in the element during the pumping stage, and that it is possible to minimize the effect of superluminescent radiation on the efficiency of pumping of an active element by reducing its thickness in the direction of the laser beam propagation.
superluminescence of a plate-shaped neodynium glass active element has an effect on the energy stored, and that this effect is greater for active elements with larger principal diagonal dimensions.
superluminescence has a significant influence on the efficiency of the pumping of plate-shaped Nd:glass active elements, and this influence is greater the smaller the size of the active element.
